title: Warrasketuck Creek
summary: Warrasketuck is a creek at Amityville on the boundary between South Oyster Bay and Babylon. The name is interpreted as the ending or point creek.
history_content: The creek functioned as part of a town-boundary landscape. Specific patent context is handled as a Timeline Entry.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Warrasketuck, Warmsketuck, Wanasketuc, Waunskittuc, and Narrasketuck. The name is interpreted as the ending or point creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Since place-names have been coined as descriptions of the features in question, or of circumstances that influenced the naming process, they are vital for the knowledge of our past.”

— Botolv Helleland, Place Names as Identity Markers (2009), Abstract

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Warrasketuck preserves a boundary-waterway name at the western edge of Babylon and the South Oyster Bay landscape.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker near the Amityville and South Oyster Bay boundary creek landscape. This is not an exact patent-boundary coordinate.
